gallery.title.situation: Heading shown above the image grid/list once the batch is non-empty (Functional Design §3.2, 'Populated state'). Sits above the mono meta line (image count and total input size) and above the toolbar row (Add images / Add folder / Clear / view mode toggle).
gallery.title.control: Static heading text, not an interactive control. Reads naturally as a possessive noun phrase in English ('Your Images'); translators are free to restructure into whatever phrasing a section title takes in the target language.

action.compressLabel.situation: Label on the single primary action button that starts a compression run (Functional Design R-A1). {count} is the number of images currently in the batch; the button is only ever shown with count >= 1, since it is disabled and unreachable when the batch is empty.
action.compressLabel.control: The one primary call-to-action button in the app: solid tint-red, always visible (panel footer on desktop, fixed bottom bar on mobile). Must read as a verb followed by a parenthesised count, e.g. 'Compress (6)' — translators should keep the count in parentheses rather than folding it into a full sentence, because it sits inside a fixed-width button, not a paragraph.

panel.section.quality.situation: Section heading above the Quality controls (target selector, slider, LOW/MED/HIGH shortcut chips) in the side panel (Functional Design §4.1). Sibling headings in the same visual family are Dimension and Format (§4.2, §4.3) — not yet added as keys, but translators should expect this word to read consistently with those when they arrive.
panel.section.quality.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking (Functional Design §14.2, 'Section headings are uppercase with wide tracking'). Not a button — do not translate as a call to action.

panel.section.dimension.situation: Section heading above the Dimension accordion (Original size / Fit within long edge / Fixed width / Fixed height rows) in the side panel (Functional Design §4.2, docs/ui-design.md §9). Sibling of panel.section.quality and panel.section.format — should read consistently with both.
panel.section.dimension.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking, same treatment as panel.section.quality. Not a button.

panel.section.format.situation: Section heading above the output-format dropdown in the side panel (Functional Design §4.3, docs/ui-design.md §10). Sibling of panel.section.quality and panel.section.dimension — should read consistently with both.
panel.section.format.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking, same treatment as panel.section.quality. Not a button.

shell.breadcrumb.selected.situation: Header breadcrumb (docs/ui-design.md §2) shown while the Gallery stage mode is mounted. {count} is the number of images currently in the batch, including zero for the empty state.
shell.breadcrumb.selected.control: Mono, uppercase (applied via CSS text-transform, not baked into this string), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.preview.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while the Preview stage mode is mounted, for the one image currently being previewed. {filename} is that image's original file name, user data, so it must not be uppercased by this template — CSS text-transform handles the surrounding label text only in visual effect, but since the whole line is one uppercase run, translators should not add casing logic around {filename} either; it renders however the surrounding CSS transform renders the whole string.
shell.breadcrumb.preview.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.edit.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while the Edit stage mode is mounted, for the image currently being rotated/cropped. {filename} is that image's original file name (user data).
shell.breadcrumb.edit.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.processing.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while a compression run is in progress (Processing stage mode).
shell.breadcrumb.processing.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.optionsButton.situation: Mobile-only header button (docs/ui-design.md §2) that opens the settings drawer. Rendered next to a decorative menu glyph (☰) that is not part of this string — the glyph is marked aria-hidden and carries no translatable text of its own.
shell.optionsButton.control: Solid tint-red pill button, same visual weight as the primary Compress action. This is the button's full visible label, so it also serves as its accessible name (R-K10) — no separate aria-label is added.

shell.hideButton.situation: Sticky button pinned to the top of the mobile settings drawer (docs/ui-design.md §2) that closes it. Rendered next to a decorative arrow glyph (→) that is not part of this string.
shell.hideButton.control: Small button at the top of the drawer's scroll area. This is the button's full visible label and accessible name (R-K10) — no separate aria-label is added.

shell.panelLabel.situation: Not visible text — the accessible name (aria-label) for the side panel landmark, used identically whether it renders as the static desktop column or the mobile drawer (docs/ui-design.md §2). Lets a screen-reader user identify the region without relying on its visual position.
shell.panelLabel.control: ARIA label on a region/dialog container, never rendered as visible text.

shell.modeNotYetBuilt.situation: Placeholder body text shown inside each of the four stage-mode components (Gallery/Preview/Edit/Processing) as built by T31, before T33-T38 give each one real content. Temporary — removed as each mode's real task lands.
shell.modeNotYetBuilt.control: Plain paragraph text inside the stage body.

gallery.emptyState.headline.situation: The large headline inside the empty-state drop zone that covers the whole stage when the batch has no images (Functional Design §3.2). Shown alongside the formats line and two Select buttons.
gallery.emptyState.headline.control: Large, bold display text, centred. Not interactive.

gallery.emptyState.formats.situation: A mono line below the empty-state headline naming the formats this build accepts as input (R-I1). Rendered as a middle-dot-separated list; translators should keep format names as their common technical abbreviations (JPEG, PNG, ...) rather than translating them, and may keep or substitute the '·' separator with whatever list punctuation reads naturally.
gallery.emptyState.formats.control: Small, quiet mono text. Not interactive.

gallery.emptyState.selectImages.situation: Primary button inside the empty-state drop zone that opens the file picker for individual images (R-I24 and its sibling flat-selection entry point).
gallery.emptyState.selectImages.control: Solid tint-red pill button, the empty state's main call to action. This is the button's full visible label and accessible name (R-K10).

gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.situation: Secondary button inside the empty-state drop zone that opens the folder picker (R-I24). Hidden entirely on a platform where folder selection is unavailable (R-I31) rather than shown disabled.
gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.control: Outlined button next to Select images. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.addImages.situation: Toolbar button in the populated Gallery state (Functional Design §3.2) that adds more individual images to the existing batch via the file picker. Same underlying action as gallery.emptyState.selectImages, different surrounding chrome (a small toolbar button rather than the empty state's large primary button), so it may read more tersely.
gallery.toolbar.addImages.control: Small outlined toolbar button. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.addFolder.situation: Toolbar button in the populated Gallery state that adds more images from a folder to the existing batch. Hidden when folder selection is unavailable (R-I31), same as gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.
gallery.toolbar.addFolder.control: Small outlined toolbar button. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.clear.situation: Toolbar button that removes every image from the batch and returns to the empty state, with no confirmation prompt (R-G6 — re-selecting files is cheap, and a confirmation dialog costs more on a touch device than the mistake it guards against).
gallery.toolbar.clear.control: Small quiet toolbar button, visually de-emphasised relative to Add images/Add folder since it is destructive. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.meta.situation: Mono meta line beneath the 'Your Images' title in the populated Gallery header, shown above both the grid and list views (docs/ui-design.md §6, 'Populated header row'). {count} is the current batch size and {size} is the total input size using the UI size formatter, never a size estimate — nothing has been compressed yet.
gallery.meta.control: Small mono text beneath the title. Not interactive.

gallery.affordance.situation: One line of guidance shown above the grid/list body in the populated Gallery header (docs/ui-design.md §6), telling the user what clicking a tile or row does before they've tried it.

gallery.badge.edited.situation: Tile/row badge shown when an image has a stored rotation or crop (R-G4). Appears first when more than one badge applies (docs/ui-design.md §6: EDITED → ANIMATED → FAILED).
gallery.badge.edited.control: Small text label with its own background, not a colour-only indicator (R-K10's colour-never-alone rule). Not interactive.

gallery.badge.animated.situation: Tile/row badge shown when the source is a multi-frame image that will be written as an animated output format. Second in display order when more than one badge applies.
gallery.badge.animated.control: Small text label with its own background, same treatment as gallery.badge.edited. Not interactive.

gallery.badge.failed.situation: Tile/row badge shown when processing failed for this image (Functional Design §10). Last in display order when more than one badge applies.
gallery.badge.failed.control: Small text label with its own background, same treatment as gallery.badge.edited. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.dimensionPending.situation: Placeholder shown in place of the W×H figure while the background dimension probe (T33-A) has not yet resolved this image's size. Replaced in place once the probe resolves or fails.
gallery.tile.dimensionPending.control: Inline text inside the tile's mono meta line. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.dimensionError.situation: Shown in place of the W×H figure when the background dimension probe could not read this image's size at all. Distinct from gallery.tile.dimensionPending — this is a terminal state, not a still-resolving one. The image itself may still be processed; only the displayed dimensions are affected.
gallery.tile.dimensionError.control: Inline text inside the tile's mono meta line. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.meta.situation: The tile's 'W×H · size' line (docs/ui-design.md §6). {dimensions} is either the real W×H figure or one of gallery.tile.dimensionPending/dimensionError, already resolved to text before this template runs; {size} uses the UI size formatter. One template per R-L5, not a concatenation of two translated fragments.
gallery.tile.meta.control: Small mono text beneath the filename. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.remove.situation: Accessible name for each tile's remove (×) control, top-right (docs/ui-design.md §6). {filename} disambiguates one tile's remove button from every other tile's in the same grid for a screen-reader user, since the visible glyph alone does not. Clicking it does not open the tile's Preview and does not affect any other tile (R-G2).
gallery.tile.remove.control: Small icon-only button with no visible text label, so this string is its aria-label rather than a redundant addition to visible text (R-K10).
